subject: thinning the result of extract(fit, permuted=TRUE)

messages.author: 1f723d378f24adbb
messages.subject: thinning the result of extract(fit, permuted=TRUE)
parts:
Hi,

If I want, say, 30 random draws from the merged postrior sample in
Rstan, what's the idiomatic way to do it?

If the result of extract(fit, permuted=TRUE) was a data.frame, I could
just use sample() and []. But since it is a list of arrays, with
generally unknown rank, I can't do that. Is there an idiomatic way that
I missed? I know how to write a function for it, just being curious.

Best,

Tamas

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] thinning the result of extract(fit, permuted=TRUE)
parts:
You can specify an amount to thin by in the original call, using
argument thin=K, which keeps every K-th draw.

If you do it after the fact from the fit in idiomatic R,
you'll need help from someone better versed in R than me.

- Bob

messages.author: da33143a8db60ce8
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] thinning the result of extract(fit, permuted=TRUE)
parts: Once you're extracting using permuted=TRUE, you should not sample at random or thin by taking every 10th or whatever, you should just take the first few in order from the permuted sample. Why? Because the permutation order gets saved, so next time you want to grab them, you'll again get the first 30 or however many draws from this permuted set.

messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] thinning the result of extract(fit, permuted=TRUE)
parts:
The other part of the question was how to operate on the list in an
idiomatic and general way in R. The problem is that all of the objects
in the list of draws are of different numbers of dimensions. So you
might have a list where the first entry was a matrix of draws and the
second a scalar.

- Bob

messages.author: 1f723d378f24adbb
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] thinning the result of extract(fit, permuted=TRUE)
parts:
I wrote have a set of utilities to deal with this problem, which I
pushed to

https://github.com/tpapp/my-stan-utils

These also include mapping functions for posteriors I was talking about
earlier. The relevant function for this problem is thin_subarrays, eg

posterior <- extract(fit, permuted=TRUE)

thinned_posterior <- thin_subarrays(posterior, 1:30)

following Andrew's suggestion to just pick the first few.

Best,

Tamas
